claim.quote: This observation of a neutrino in spatial coincidence with a gamma-ray emitting blazar during an active phase suggests that blazars may be a source of high-energy neutrinos.

date.note: arXiv v1 submission date. Published as Science 361, eaat1378 (2018).

name: Multimessenger observation of blazar TXS 0506+056 with IceCube-170922A
notes: The paper is authored jointly by IceCube and the Fermi-LAT, MAGIC, AGILE, ASAS-SN, HAWC, H.E.S.S., INTEGRAL, Kanata, Kiso, Kapteyn, Liverpool, Subaru, Swift/NuSTAR, VERITAS and VLA teams; only collaboration:icecube exists in the atlas so far.

significance.note: The abstract states no significance. The companion paper (arXiv:1807.08794) reports 3.5σ evidence for an earlier neutrino flare from the same direction.

summary.plain: A single very energetic neutrino arrived from the direction of a distant galaxy with a jet pointed at us, just as telescopes saw that galaxy flaring in gamma rays. It was the first time a likely source of a cosmic neutrino was pinned down.
summary.technical: The 290 TeV track alert IceCube-170922A was spatially coincident with the flaring gamma-ray blazar TXS 0506+056. A multiwavelength campaign across radio to VHE gamma rays characterised the flare, including the first VHE gamma-ray detection of the source.

title: Multi-messenger observations of a flaring blazar coincident with high-energy neutrino IceCube-170922A
why_it_matters: First identification of a candidate astrophysical source of high-energy neutrinos and a founding result of multimessenger astronomy with neutrinos.
